[USER] User expressed interest in the role of probability in quantum mechanics.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Probability plays a fundamental role in quantum mechanics as it allows predictions to be made about the behavior of subatomic particles.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The behavior of particles is determined by wave functions, which describe the probability of the particle being in a particular location or having a particular energy.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The probability of a specific outcome is determined by taking the square of the absolute value of the wave function, called the probability density.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The probability density can be used to calculate the probability of finding a particle in a particular location or having a particular energy.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The uncertainty principle states that it is impossible to measure both the position and momentum of a particle with absolute precision.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Measuring one property affects the other, and the uncertainty can only be described in terms of probability.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Probability is critical in quantum mechanics as it allows predictions about the behavior of subatomic particles and provides a more complete understanding of the quantum world.  
[USER] User found the information fascinating and inquired if probability plays a role in all quantum mechanical systems or only specific ones.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Probability plays a role in all quantum mechanical systems.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The quantum state of any physical system is described by a wave function, which encodes all the information about the system.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Unlike classical mechanics, the wave function gives a probabilistic prediction of the system's behavior.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The probability of a particular outcome can be determined by calculating the square of the absolute value of the wave function.  
[USER] User asked if quantum mechanics is more of a probabilistic theory than a deterministic one like classical mechanics.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Quantum mechanics is inherently probabilistic, in contrast to classical mechanics, which is fundamentally deterministic.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The wave function gives a probability distribution of possible outcomes for a measurement or observation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Richard Feynman stated, "Nature does not know what you are looking at, and she behaves accordingly."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics is central to phenomena like the Heisenberg uncertainty principle, wave-particle duality, and quantum entanglement.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Despite its probabilistic nature, quantum mechanics allows for precise predictions of experimental results, verified by numerous experiments.
